styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hawker centres, kopitiam breakfasts and late-night satay.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Chinatown, Little India, Kampong Glam and the museums.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Gardens, the zoo and Sentosa with the kids.

stays.why: Walk to Gardens by the Bay, the Merlion and the bay lights. Best for first-timers who want the skyline at night.
Malls on your doorstep and a central MRT line. Good for shoppers and easy taxi rides anywhere.
Hawker food, temples and shophouse hotels. Cheaper than the bay and close to the river.
Lively street market, good MRT links and short walks to Kampong Glam and Little India.

food: Eat at hawker centres: Maxwell, Lau Pa Sat and Old Airport Road. A meal is often SGD 4–8.
Start the day with kaya toast, soft-boiled eggs and kopi at a kopitiam.
Try chilli crab, laksa, chicken rice and char kway teow. Prices vary widely by stall.
Many stalls are cash-only or use local payment apps. Carry small notes.
Book popular restaurants ahead. Hawker queues are shortest before noon and after 2pm.
more_time: Swap a mall afternoon for a walk in the Botanic Gardens, free and open early.
Take a short ferry to Pulau Ubin or the Southern Islands for a slower day; check timings on the day.
Add a half-day in Kampong Glam and Little India for temples, murals and cheap eats.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the bay, the old quarters and one Sentosa or nature day without rushing in the heat.

month_notes: Jan: hot and wet, about 24 rain days. Plan indoor backups.
Feb: the driest month, around 18 rain days. Good for outdoor days.
Mar: wet again, about 25 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
Apr: very wet, about 27 rain days. Short heavy showers are common.
May: the wettest month, about 28 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
Jun: still wet, about 26 rain days. Mornings are often clearer.
Jul: slightly drier, about 23 rain days. Hot and humid all day.
Aug: wet, about 26 rain days. Watch for afternoon storms.
Sep: about 23 rain days. Similar to July, hot and muggy.
Oct: wet, about 27 rain days. Indoor sights are a safe bet.
Nov: very wet, about 28 rain days. Expect downpours.
Dec: very wet, about 28 rain days. Pack rain gear and light layers.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year: highs near 29–30°C, lows near 24–25°C, and rain on most months.

items.title: Warm every month
items.text: Highs stay around 29–30°C and lows around 24–25°C. No cool season.

items.title: Rain is common
items.text: Expect 18–28 rain days a month. February is the driest; May, November and December are the wettest.

items.title: Short heavy showers
items.text: Downpours often pass quickly. Carry a small umbrella and use covered walkways.

items.title: High humidity
items.text: It feels hotter than the numbers. Drink water and take breaks in air-conditioning.

items.title: Best outdoor months
items.text: February and July–September have fewer rain days. Still plan around afternoon storms.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sandals or quick-dry shoes, an umbrella and sunscreen. A light layer for cold indoor AC.

transit.best: MRT for most trips; ride apps or metered taxis for late nights and door-to-door.

modes.text: MRT trains are fast and cheap. Tap a contactless credit card or buy an EZ-link card.
Buses cover gaps the MRT misses. Fares are distance-based and low.
Taxis meter fares. Grab and Gojek ride apps are widely used.
Driving is possible but costly: ERP tolls, high parking and a car-ownership tax regime.
Walking is pleasant in the core. Covered walkways help in rain and heat.
Ferries run from HarbourFront and Tanah Merah to the Riau Islands and Johor.
